title: Menachem ben Signai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Mishnah Eduyot ch. 7, mishnah 8: he testified concerning the extension of the cauldron of olive-boilers, that it is impure, and that of dyers, that it is pure. And in the Tosefta there, at the beginning of ch. 3, [it is related] that he was a dyer, and when they seated him in the academy, everyone was astonished at him; he said to them: such and such [may befall me] if I am not the head of all who come after me (so it reads in the Zuckermandel Tosefta).

And in the Introduction to the Mishnah, p. 233, [the author] conjectures that he was called Ben Signai for this reason, based on Mishnah Kelim ch. 5, mishnah 4, [which says] that these craftsmen had ovens in the village of Signai, and he was named after the village in which he lived.

notes.text: מוסף היורה is the cauldron’s extension or added rim. רפ״ג means the beginning of chapter 3.
The words “if I am not” are explicit in אם איני. Only the imprecation “such and such [may befall me]” is supplied. Hyman attributes this reading to Zuckermandel’s Tosefta.
The conjecture about the name Signai is attributed to the Introduction to the Mishnah, cited on page 233. Hyman does not name its author.

The cauldron’s extension is its added rim. The consulted Machon Mamre Tosefta Eduyot 3 names Menachem ben Pubagi and has a different oath formula. Hyman reports Signai and “if I am not” from the Zuckermandel edition, which was not independently inspected here. The village explanation remains a conjecture.
